newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GVT PARTY SAYS IN NEUTRALITY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GVT PARTY SAYS IN NEUTRALITY TALKS.

text.p: The Slovak National Party (SNS) a member of the ruling coalition, said on Monday it had discussed the country's possible neutrality with Russia and was planning talks with the United States on the same issue.
In a debate on independent radio Twist, SNS chairman Jan Slota said the Russian ambassador to Bratislava Sergei Zotov had already promised Russian support on the matter.
"We directly asked ambassador Zotov for a possible Russian reaction to Slovak requests for neutrality guarantees...and we received a positive answer," Slota said.
Russia has repeatedly stated its opposition to the eastern expansion of NATO and has called the alliance obsolete.

"Membership of NATO would be a catastrophe for Slovakia," added Slota whose senior coalition partner, the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) of Premier Vladimir Meciar, has declared itself in favour of NATO membership.

Slovakia has officially declared its intention to be among the first new members of the alliance, but its chances appear to have waned in recent months after repeated U.S. and European Union criticism of the pace of its democratic reforms.
Slota said Meciar had accepted the SNS position.
"The premier... accepts differences among the members of the coalition," Slota said.

Last week Meciar conceded that Slovakia was unlikely to be among the first countries to be invited to join the alliance when NATO holds a summit in Madrid in July, mainly blaming the United States and its "negative" attitude towards Slovakia.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, asked last week in Bratislava if Russia would favour Slovak neutrality, said: "...we would support any solution oriented this way."
Slota, an anti-NATO and EU hardliner, said the SNS would seek U.S. approval for Slovak neutrality.
"We realise that one-sided guarantees are insufficient for neutrality... therefore I want to contact the U.S. ambassador soon to discuss the issue with him," he said.
Slovakia, which became independent when Czechoslovakia split in 1993, is planning to hold a referendum on May 23 and 24 on whether to join NATO.
